title: Letta Code with a local model
description: Letta Code with a model on your own server (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM or another OpenAI-compatible one) and nothing else: only the server's address is opened, and its long-term memory stays in the sandbox.

de.title: Letta Code mit einem lokalen Modell
de.description: Letta Code mit einem Modell auf Ihrem eigenen Server (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM oder ein anderer OpenAI-kompatibler) und sonst nichts: nur die Adresse des Servers ist offen, und sein Langzeitgedächtnis bleibt in der Sandbox.

llm.label: LLM server (sandbox-ai llm list), NAME or NAME:MODEL
llm.hint: sandbox-ai llm add ollama --kind ollama --url http://127.0.0.1:11434 --model MODEL

notes: Register the server once: sandbox-ai llm add NAME --kind ollama|lmstudio|llamacpp|vllm|openai-compatible --url URL --model MODEL; sandbox-ai llm check NAME --agent letta asks it for the API Letta Code uses.

Letta Code gets the server as variables: its OpenAI-compatible provider llama-cpp at the server's /v1 URL (LLAMA_CPP_BASE_URL) with the key as a placeholder the connection proxy replaces, and --model llama-cpp/MODEL. LM Studio, Ollama, vLLM and llama.cpp all work.

The relay sets the model's parameters (sandbox-ai llm params) and the loop guard on the wire, the same for every agent; Letta Code has no read-only place for the loop guard's instructions or a turn limit. Agents need a model with tool calls and a long context (qwen3-coder, gpt-oss, ...; Ollama: OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=32768 or more). On this host's loopback (http://127.0.0.1:PORT) only with Podman.
Letta Code's memory subagents (reflection, dreaming) use the same model: a small one may take a while between turns.
Its image first: sandbox-ai build letta.
